Lemma
[Inward boundary fixed-point criterion] 1. ch11:11.7\group gt-ch11 Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0298 Let $B$ be the open unit ball in $\B $. If $T:\overline B\to \B $ is continuous, $T(\overline B)$ is precompact, and $T(\partial B)\subset B$, then $T$ has a fixed point.
Proof

\sketch Radially retract $T$ to $\overline B$ and apply Corollary 1. A fixed point on the sphere would contradict $T(\partial B)\subset B$, so the retraction is inactive at the fixed point.

□

For a family \[ Q_\sigma u=a^{ij}(x,u,Du;\sigma )D_{ij}u+b(x,u,Du;\sigma ), \] assume:

  1. $Q_1=Q$ and $b(x,z,p;0)=0$;

  2. each $Q_\sigma $ is elliptic;

  3. $a^{ij}$ and $b$ depend continuously on $\sigma $ as $C^\alpha (\overline\Omega \times \mathbb R\times \mathbb R^n)$ functions.
